clue.text: HS2's plans: official reports describe detailed electric transportation

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed, so the word it qualifies loses its final letter
to describe is to draw a line around something, so one word encircles another

blocks.note: bulletins are official news statements
a tram is an electrically powered street vehicle

explanation.surface: Official documents lay out the plans for Britain's HS2 electric railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as thorough, but it means cut off at the tail. HS2 is a planned British high-speed railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: HS2 is a high-speed rail project, so the fast trains it plans to run are bullet trains in the Japanese style.

clue.text: Spoke, and mumbled, without mumbling at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it
without means lacking, so a letter is removed from the other word

blocks.note: to mutter is to speak in a low indistinct voice
the opening letter of mumbling

explanation.surface: Someone spoke, mumbling at first and then less so.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter something is to say it out loud, a straightforward synonym for having spoken.

clue.text: Um... I'd like to have a look at that

definitions.text: I'd like to have a look at that

blocks.note: first meaning: a hesitating filler phrase while thinking

blocks.clueFragment: I'd like to have a look at that
blocks.note: second meaning: a request to be shown something

explanation.walkthrough: The same three-word phrase is both a stalling noise while you think and a literal request to see something.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works as a thinking pause, like um, and as a polite request asking to inspect an object.

clue.text: Also, knight removed from chessboard

blocks.note: too means as well
K is the abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight is also taken off the board in a chess game.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess notation the knight is N, but in crosswords knight is usually K, as in titles like KBE.
explanation.definitionFit: When a chess player captures an opponent's piece, they are said to have taken it, lifting it off play.

clue.text: Taking last two slices, bistro guest ate in country, not respecting others

indicators.note: only the final two pieces of the first word are kept, the rest being thrown away

blocks.note: the word as written, of which only the end is wanted
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner at a bistro tucks into the last two slices, ignoring everyone else at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's rude diner is mirrored by the definition: a nation that ignores international rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue state is a nation regarded as flouting international law and threatening its neighbours.

clue.text: Make horizontal axis the reverse of what you'd expect

definitions.text: the reverse of what you'd expect

blocks.note: to iron something is to press it flat
the y-axis of a graph

explanation.surface: An instruction for drawing a graph, which is then oddly said to be counter-intuitive.
explanation.walkthrough: There is a little joke here: the y-axis is the vertical one, so making it horizontal is itself contrary.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony describes a situation whose outcome is opposite to what was anticipated or intended.

clue.text: 'Good to enter into unrestrained nudism': big name in psychoanalysis

indicators.note: unrestrained suggests letters let loose to run in any order
entering into something means going inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A quotation recommending wild naturism, attributed to a famous psychoanalyst.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigmund Freud founded psychoanalysis, so his first name is a celebrated figure in that field.

clue.text: Somehow, seaport usable for vessels used only for fun

indicators.note: somehow says the letters get there by some unstated rearrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A harbour turns out to be suitable for leisure craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure boats are craft kept for recreation and outings rather than trade or fishing work.

clue.text: Pershing felt a worry, creating machines of war

indicators.note: to worry something is to tug and shake it about, disturbing the letters

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: General Pershing feels anxious while building an arsenal.
explanation.walkthrough: Pershing was an American First World War general, and 'worry' looks like his feeling, not an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighter planes are combat aircraft, military machines built for air battles.

clue.text: Disney tune the French singer's getting to at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of each word just before it

blocks.note: le is French for the
a tit is a small songbird
the closing letter of getting
the closing letter of to

explanation.surface: A French singer finally gets round to a Disney song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' looks like a performer but is a bird; crosswords often use singer for a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: Let It Go is the famous song from the Disney film Frozen.

clue.text: Hanover king, egregious lunatic after losing America

indicators.note: losing something means letters are taken away from the word
lunatic means crazy, so the letters are jumbled madly

blocks.note: taken as written
US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A Hanoverian king behaves outrageously after losing the American colonies.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes George III, who lost America and was thought mad, but the answer is his great-grandfather.
explanation.definitionFit: George I was the first British monarch from the German House of Hanover, reigning from 1714.

clue.text: Get on... get on... about... about...

indicators.note: the second about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to get on is to grow older
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone stammering out instructions, repeating themselves in a dither.
explanation.walkthrough: Each phrase is repeated with a different job: one get on is the definition, the other is the letters; one about is letters, the other wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: People who get on well have harmonious relations, so they agree with each other.

clue.text: Final half of bowling, champ's losing heart a lot

indicators.note: only the closing half of the next word is kept, the first half dropped
losing its heart means the middle letter is removed

blocks.note: a delivery is a single ball bowled in cricket
to champ is to chew noisily, to munch

explanation.surface: A bowling champion's final innings sees them lose their nerve badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champ' suggests a champion but is the verb to chew. In cricket a delivery is one ball sent down by the bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Very much and a lot are interchangeable adverbial phrases meaning greatly or to a large degree.

clue.text: Become a success, capable of recompense

definitions.note: a verb here: to make amends

blocks.note: to make it is to succeed
up to a task means able to do it

explanation.surface: Someone who has made good is now able to pay people back.
explanation.definitionFit: To make it up to someone is to compensate them for a wrong done, which is recompensing them.

clue.text: Rashly, he sued aunt for carelessness

indicators.note: done rashly, without care, so the letters are thrown together anyhow

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man impulsively takes his aunt to court for negligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue haste is excessive hurry, the kind of rushing that leads to mistakes and negligence.

clue.text: Vain and regularly indulged

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of indulged

explanation.surface: A conceited person who is habitually pampered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vain' looks like conceited, but here it means futile, as in an idle threat.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean without purpose or effect, as vain does in phrases like idle or vain boasts.

clue.text: Enormous jerk about to commit sin with one female

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the rest

blocks.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch
to err is to do wrong
I is the Roman numeral for one
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A huge idiot is about to sin with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult for a person, but it is a twitch. Terrific originally meant terrifying, hence huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrific can mean of great size or intensity, as in a terrific noise, so it matches enormous.

clue.text: Dutch specialty that's made round?

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, read from end to start

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Dutch delicacy which is produced in a round shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: Edam really is made in round balls, so 'round' does double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild cheese from the Netherlands, named after the town where it originated.

clue.text: American cinema, oddly uninspiring

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters are set out strangely

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic's verdict that Hollywood films are curiously dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' could suggest taking odd letters, but those give no answer; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemic figuratively means lacking vigour or colour, so something weak and dull, which is uninspiring.

clue.text: To be summarily dismissed, you might do this at the butcher's counter

definitions.text: you might do this at the butcher's counter

blocks.note: first meaning: to be sacked without ceremony

blocks.clueFragment: you might do this at the butcher's counter
blocks.note: second meaning, playful: to buy a cut of meat from the butcher

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic definition taking the idiom literally, as buying a pork or lamb chop.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be fired abruptly, while literally it describes purchasing a cut of meat.

clue.text: One caught in childhood game wearing quaint socks

indicators.note: a thing being worn is enclosed by the garment around it

blocks.note: hose is an old-fashioned word for stockings or socks
tag is a chasing game played by children

explanation.surface: A child playing a game in old-fashioned socks gets caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quaint' tells you the word for socks is dated: hose, as in Shakespearean doublet and hose.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person seized and held captive as security, someone captured.

clue.text: A polenta stew requiring next to no effort

indicators.note: a stew is a mixed-up jumble, so the letters are stirred about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe for a polenta stew that is very easy to make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' looks like the dish but is the anagram signal; the plate also fits the cooking picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handed to you on a plate comes with no work needed, an idiom for easily obtained.

clue.text: Behold! First half of pulpit address delivers one that's been left behind

indicators.note: only the opening half of the next phrase's word is kept, the rest dropped

blocks.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look
a sermon is a talk given from a church pulpit

explanation.surface: A preacher's sermon proclaims something about the forsaken.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is someone beaten in a contest, the competitor trailing and outpaced by others.

clue.text: Sun god's receiving thanks from worshipper

blocks.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god, with the S of the possessive
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A sun god is being thanked by one of his devotees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worshipper' suggests the sun god's follower, but it is a Rastafarian, who worships Haile Selassie.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rasta, short for Rastafarian, follows a religion revering the Ethiopian emperor Haile Selassie.

clue.text: Element derived from quartz in compounds

indicators.note: derived from says the letters are drawn out of the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of quartz, all of in and the start of compounds

explanation.surface: A chemical element obtained from compounds of quartz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal, but it is just part of the run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a metallic chemical element, atomic number 30.

clue.text: Original impetus for feminist campaign

indicators.note: original means novel or freshly made, so the letters are formed into something new

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: What first sparked a women's rights movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like a history question, but 'Original' is the anagram signal and only the campaign is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Time's Up is a 2018 movement, founded by Hollywood women, against sexual harassment in the workplace.

clue.text: Actually, half-missing dearly departed balloon

indicators.note: with half missing, only the first half of the word survives

blocks.note: in fact means actually
the late is a term for someone who has died

explanation.surface: A grieving remark about a lost loved one, oddly tied to a balloon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balloon' looks like a noun but is the verb to swell.
explanation.definitionFit: To balloon is to swell up rapidly, which is what something does when you inflate it.

clue.text: Atmospheric processes produced by automobiles overtaking bishop on bike

indicators.note: a vehicle overtaking passes alongside, here read as going around the rest

blocks.note: cars are automobiles
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
taken as written
a cycle is a bicycle

explanation.surface: Cars passing a cycling bishop pump out exhaust into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface links cars to emissions, fittingly, since they feed carbon into the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon cycles are the natural exchanges of carbon between air, oceans, rocks and living things.
